purpose: Mathematical Model Registry (17A.4): structured representations of physical systems, distinct from — and linked to — the 63-equation registry. Lifecycle statuses distinguish documented-only references from executable, verified and validated models.
classification_notes: model_class values: analytical-theoretical | semi-empirical | mechanistic-physical | numerical-simulation | machine-learning. Equations ≠ models: a model composes governing equations + assumptions + conditions + closure.

environment_profiles.label: Lunar habitat (concept)
environment_profiles.habitat_vs_exterior: PROFILE = pressurised inhabited habitat; the exterior lunar/Martian surface has no breathable oxidiser atmosphere and is NOT a combustion environment for these models

environment_profiles.label: Mars habitat (concept)
environment_profiles.habitat_vs_exterior: PROFILE = pressurised inhabited habitat; the exterior lunar/Martian surface has no breathable oxidiser atmosphere and is NOT a combustion environment for these models

ranking_policy: Candidate ranking uses documented policy tiers, no invented probabilities: (1) environment compatibility (direct > modified > qualitative; not-applicable excluded), (2) validation tier (EXPERIMENTALLY_VALIDATED > PARTIALLY_VALIDATED > CODE_VERIFIED > DOCUMENTED_ONLY), (3) output/phenomenon match, (4) executable before documented. Full breakdown shown per selection.

models.name: Ideal-gas habitat atmosphere state
intended_applications: Habitat/cabin atmosphere characterisation for flammability and suppression analysis
Oxygen partial pressure and density at any selected environment
models.description: Composes the ideal-gas law, Dalton partial pressures, mean molecular weight and ideal-gas density to fully characterise a pressurised atmosphere from (O2 fraction, total pressure, temperature). The flammability-relevant output is oxygen partial pressure, which the challenge documentation identifies as the primary flammability variable.
assumptions: Ideal-gas behaviour (all habitat pressures are far above critical)
Binary O2/N2 approximation for density unless full composition given

applicability_limits.note: Exact within ideal-gas assumptions; flammability interpretation still requires fuel-specific limits
applicability_limits.exterior_moon_mars: NOT applicable to exterior lunar/Martian near-vacuum surfaces (no pressurised oxidiser atmosphere)

source_references.source: challenge brief — Moon-base ≥30% O2 at ≤10.2 psi

experimental_validation.note: equation registry reference tests (p-o2-kpa: Earth 21.28 kPa, Moon 21.10 kPa)

models.verification_status: CODE_VERIFIED (68/68 registry reference tests pass; re-run via /api/selftest)
limitations: Does not model reaction chemistry or flow

models.name: Buoyancy-ventilation transport regime scaling
intended_applications: Classifying which transport mechanism (buoyancy / ventilation / diffusion) dominates a flame at a given gravity and flow
Justifying why terrestrial data does or does not transfer to microgravity
models.description: Reduced-order scaling model: computes characteristic buoyant velocity (sqrt(g) scaling), Grashof/Rayleigh numbers, Richardson number and Froude number, then classifies the flame transport regime. In microgravity the buoyant velocity collapses and diffusion/ventilation dominates — the single most important environment distinction in the corpus.

environmental_domain.note: regime classification changes across gravity: diffusion-limited (µg) → mixed (partial-g) → buoyancy-dominated (1g)

applicability_limits.note: Scaling relations only — no flame geometry, chemistry or radiation; regime labels are qualitative guidance

source_references.source: NASA FLT lower-body negative pressure / flame-shape scaling discussion; Turns Ch. fluids (scaling laws)

experimental_validation.note: registry test vectors (Earth Ri 261.5; µg Ri → 2.6e-4)

uncertainty_information.extras: regime boundaries (factor-3 velocity comparisons) are heuristic

limitations: Scaling relations cannot predict flame shape or spread rate
Regime boundaries are heuristic factor comparisons

models.name: Classical d²-law droplet combustion (quasi-steady, spherically symmetric)
intended_applications: Microgravity isolated-droplet burning (FLEX/CFI regime)
Droplet lifetime estimation from d0 and burning rate K
First-order extinction-diameter trajectory
models.description: Classical quasi-steady droplet-combustion model (Godsave 1953; Spalding 1953): in microgravity the flame is spherically symmetric and the droplet diameter decreases linearly in time, d² = d0² − K·t, until extinction (d_ext) or burnout. K is the burning-rate constant set by vaporisation-diffusion balance (Spalding B number). The model composes the registry's d2-law, burning-rate-constant, droplet-lifetime and spalding-b-number equations.
physical_principles: Spalding transfer number B links burning rate to thermochemistry
assumptions: Constant K (no time-varying transport, no disruptive burning)
No radiation correction (radiation matters for cool flames / large droplets)
material_properties: ambient O2/N2/He/CO composition (affects B and K)

environmental_domain.gravity: ≤0.02 g direct (spherical); partial-g qualitative (buoyant distortion); 1-g qualitative

applicability_limits.cool_flames: does NOT capture cool-flame two-stage burning (see cool-flame-two-stage model)

source_references.source: Turns, An Introduction to Combustion, Ch. 10 (droplet burning)
PSI-69 FLEX recovered table (K, d0, t_burn, d_ext)

Heptane.lit_range_note: classical microgravity droplet-burning K is commonly O(0.5-1.5) mm^2/s for methanol/heptane at these conditions

Methanol.lit_range_note: classical microgravity droplet-burning K is commonly O(0.5-1.5) mm^2/s for methanol/heptane at these conditions

experimental_validation.interpretation: Constant-K d²-law reproduces the recovered FLEX K values within literature order-of-magnitude (µg K medians 0.46-0.54 mm²/s, reduced vs 1g as expected from weaker convective transport) but FAILS to predict individual burn times quantitatively (MAE 7.9-10.3 s, RMSE 10.4-19.0 s) — constant-K idealisation does not hold per-test (time-varying K, disruption events, dilution-dependent extinction). Use as first-order trajectory only.

calibration_information.note: K is a measured input per test (recovered table), not a fitted global parameter; per-fuel medians quoted as calibration context only

uncertainty_information.extras: per-test variability dominates; see lifetime_prediction MAE/RMSE

models.verification_status: CODE_VERIFIED (registry test vectors: d0=3, K=0.8 → d(4s)=5.8 mm; t_life=11.25 s)

models.name: Thermally-thick solid ignition under constant radiant flux
intended_applications: 1-g bench flammability screening (BASS-class radiant ignition)
Ignition-time estimate from thermal inertia k*rho*c and incident flux
models.description: Semi-infinite solid heated by constant net flux ignites at t_ig = (pi/4)·(k*rho*c)·(T_ig − T_inf)²/q''² (thermally-thick regime). Composes the registry's ignition-time-thick, critical-heat-flux and thermal-inertia equations. The gravity term does not appear explicitly: ignition is conduction-limited into the solid, so the formulation transfers to other gravities qualitatively — but heat feedback from the flame (which DOES depend on gravity) is outside this model.
physical_principles: Thermal inertia k*rho*c as the ignition-resistance property
assumptions: Thermally thick (ignition before thermal penetration of the full sample thickness)
Constant net flux (no flame feedback during preheat)

environmental_domain.gravity: gravity-independent formulation (conduction-limited); flame heat-feedback stage is gravity-dependent and NOT modelled

applicability_limits.microgravity: preheat conduction transfers directly; the subsequent flame-spread stage requires spread models — ignition time alone is transferable qualitatively
applicability_limits.thermally_thin: invalid for thin fabrics where Biot/penetration covers the sample (use thermally-thin formulation)

source_references.source: Drysdale, An Introduction to Fire Dynamics 3rd ed. (thermally-thick ignition)

experimental_validation.note: BASS-II table records ignition times per test — future work: fit k*rho*c per material and compare (input completeness: sample dimensions + flux recorded)

uncertainty_information.extras: T_ig criterion and constant-flux idealisation dominate

models.name: Aerosol settling / diffusion scaling (Stokes + Cunningham)
intended_applications: Contrast 1-g vs microgravity smoke transport for detector placement
Settling velocity and Brownian-diffusion scaling per particle size
models.description: Combines Stokes settling velocity (with Cunningham slip correction) and Brownian diffusivity to characterise smoke-particle transport. In 1 g, settling dominates for >1 µm particles; in microgravity, settling vanishes and Brownian diffusion + ventilation dominate — the physical basis of the SAME/SAME-R finding that spacecraft smoke behaves differently and detectors must be validated in the flight regime.
physical_principles: Cunningham slip correction for sub-micron particles

environmental_domain.gravity: any (g is an explicit input; µg → v_s → 0 and diffusion dominates)

applicability_limits.note: Single-particle scaling — no coagulation, agglomeration, electrostatics or ventilation transport
applicability_limits.same_note: SAME/SAME-R measured the actual size distributions (corpus PSI-101/102)

experimental_validation.note: registry test vectors; SAME/SAME-R provide the measured distributions the scaling operates on

uncertainty_information.extras: shape factor and size distribution spread dominate

models.validation_status: validated_against_reference_tests (scaling identities; distribution data external to model)
limitations: Detection-time estimation requires ventilation field (not modelled)

models.name: Froude-scaling of opposed-flow flame spread
intended_applications: Scaling spread-rate comparisons between gravity levels and flow speeds (qualitative)
Explaining why 1-g spread data does not transfer directly to microgravity
models.description: Semi-empirical scaling: opposed-flow flame spread over thin fuels correlates with the flow Froude number Fr = U²/(gL) — as gravity decreases, buoyancy-induced mixing weakens and the spread rate departs from 1-g correlations. The registry's froude-number and froude-spread-scaling equations give the dimensionless spread rate V*. Quantitative prediction requires fuel-specific empirical constants; the scaling itself is qualitative across gravities.
physical_principles: Froude-number similarity of buoyant opposed-flow spread
assumptions: Empirical constants per fuel/thickness not included

environmental_domain.gravity: 1e-6 to 1 g (the scaling's subject); quantitative constants exist only for the tested 1-g/flow combinations

applicability_limits.microgravity: in µg the buoyant scale collapses — spread is flow- or radiation-controlled, outside this correlation's calibrated domain
applicability_limits.note: SAFFIRE large-scale µg spread is the experimental reference, not this scaling

source_references.source: Drysdale (flame-spread scaling); NASA microgravity spread literature

experimental_validation.note: SAFFIRE/1-g spread-rate columns in PSI-99 support future per-fuel fitting — recorded as future work

limitations: No quantitative prediction without fuel-specific constants
Not valid in µg limit for absolute rates

models.name: FLEX droplet-extinction classifier v2 (ML)
intended_applications: Extinction-outcome classification for isolated droplets under diluent atmospheres (FLEX regime)
Suppression screening for CO2/He dilution of droplet flames
models.description: Six-feature logistic-regression classifier predicting visible-flame extinction for isolated methanol/heptane droplets from pre-test conditions (fuel, d0, pressure, O2/N2/CO/He). Registered here in the ML category to keep the model-type distinction explicit; scoring lives in src/lib/science/models.ts and the existing Model Studio playground.
physical_principles: Empirical statistical boundary learned from recovered FLEX tests
Pre-test features only (no leakage of outcome columns)
governing_equations: logistic(p) = sigma(w·x + b) on standardised features
assumptions: Outcome = visible-flame extinction recorded in test end

applicability_limits.uncalibrated: score is relative, not a probability

source_references.source: PSI-69 FLEX recovered table (training data, SHA-256)

calibration_information.note: NOT probability-calibrated — output labelled UNCALIBRATED relative score

models.name: CFI-G hot-ignition scorer (ML, exploratory)
intended_applications: Exploratory hot-ignition scoring for CFI-G inverse-flame conditions
Transparency example: honest negative/exploratory result retained
models.description: Spec-preserved logistic coefficients scoring hot-ignition outcome for CFI-G inverse-flame gaseous conditions. Registered as EXPLORATORY: it does NOT outperform the single-feature oxygen baseline under grouped validation (recorded AUC 0.682 vs 0.728) and is retained for transparency — not for decisions.
physical_principles: Empirical statistical boundary on gaseous cool/hot-flame transition features

applicability_limits.exploratory: below oxygen-only baseline — do not use for decisions

models.verification_status: CODE_VERIFIED (validated against recovered rows: 146 usable / 131 positives exact match)
models.validation_status: EXPLORATORY (below baseline — retained as honest negative result)

models.name: Two-stage ignition / negative-temperature-coefficient cool-flame model (literature)
intended_applications: Explaining CFI-G two-stage ignition and cool-flame persistence
Reference formulation for low-temperature kinetic modelling
models.description: Low-temperature kinetic model of two-stage ignition: first-stage (cool-flame) heat release from RO₂/QOOH branching chemistry followed by negative-temperature-coefficient behaviour and delayed hot ignition. DOCUMENTED ONLY: the governing kinetic scheme lives in the cited literature; no numerical solver is implemented in ZERO FLARE.
governing_equations: elementary low-temperature kinetic steps (see sources; not re-registered here)
assumptions: 0-D homogeneous or 1-D diffusion formulation per source

applicability_limits.note: Quantitative use requires an implemented kinetic solver — out of ZERO FLARE scope

source_references.source: 1-s2.0-S0016236115011758-am.pdf (Zhao et al., Initiation and Propagation of Laminar Premixed Cool Flames)

experimental_validation.note: source publications validate against their own experiments — not re-validated in ZERO FLARE

limitations: No executable solver in ZERO FLARE

models.name: Flamelet-Generated-Manifold concurrent flame-spread modelling (literature / PSI-62)
intended_applications: Reference numerical formulation for concurrent (opposed + cocurrent) flame spread over solid fuels
PSI-62 investigation's own modelling approach
models.description: PSI-62 (Concurrent Flame Spread Modeling using Flamelet Generated Manifolds) applies FGM-reduced chemistry with CFD to model concurrent flame spread. DOCUMENTED ONLY: the modelling approach and its validation live in the investigation's publications; ZERO FLARE implements no FGM/CFD solver.
physical_principles: Flamelet-generated manifolds for turbulent/premixed-diffusion chemistry reduction
Concurrent spread coupling of opposed and cocurrent flows

applicability_limits.note: Requires a full CFD stack — explicitly out of ZERO FLARE scope; never claim these charts/animations are CFD

source_references.source: PSI-62 investigation record (Concurrent Flame Spread Modeling using FGM)

experimental_validation.note: PSI-62 publications carry their own validation

limitations: CFD-boundary: never label UI charts/3D as CFD

models.name: ISS Fine Water Mist suppression (heat extraction / dilution mechanisms)
intended_applications: Explaining water-mist suppression mechanisms for spacecraft firefighting
Qualitative suppression-system assessment (agent transport, heat extraction, dilution)
models.description: Mechanistic suppression model family for fine water mist: droplet evaporation heat extraction, oxygen dilution by steam, and radiative blocking, with microgravity transport differences (no buoyant delivery; mist travels by momentum only). DOCUMENTED ONLY: the AIAA/ESA sources document the ISS FWM system development and tests; no suppression solver is implemented here. Quantitative suppression-effectiveness ranking is refused by design (tests are not condition-matched).
governing_equations: extinction criterion via dilution/cooling (no closed form registered here)

environmental_domain.gravity: µg (ISS) — transport differs fundamentally from 1g sprays

applicability_limits.note: No suppressant ranking is offered (tests not condition-matched — see suppressant gap)
applicability_limits.earth_transfer: FWM spin-off to terrestrial firefighting documented in sources
